clue.text: Vehicle going fast with Shell

blocks.note: a car is an everyday vehicle
apace means at speed, quickly

explanation.surface: A car speeding along, perhaps with a Shell petrol logo on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell looks like the oil company; it is the definition, a hard outer casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard protective upper casing of a tortoise, crab or beetle.

clue.text: Club with clergy membership

blocks.note: first meaning: a famous London gaming club
second meaning: the directory listing every Church of England clergyman

explanation.surface: A gentlemen's club whose members are all vicars.
explanation.walkthrough: Crockford's is a London casino club, and Crockford's Clerical Directory lists Anglican clergy; the two share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The same proper name belongs to an exclusive gambling establishment and to the reference book recording ordained Anglicans.

clue.text: After reverse, Gordius - inter alia - gets his own back

indicators.note: a reverse runs backwards, so the word and the set are read from right to left

blocks.note: after, subsequently
the setter refers to himself
among other things, loosely one of a set

explanation.surface: The setter, among other people, takes revenge after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose Gordius clue: the setter is I, and 'inter alia' is read as one among a set; both the word for after and the set are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to strike back at someone who has harmed you, taking revenge.

clue.text: Bird parts with a pound for a nut

indicators.note: to part with something is to give it up, so letters are dropped

blocks.note: a large water bird with a pouched bill
a, one, the Roman numeral
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: A bird gives up money to buy a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird loses its middle two letters, the pound sign and one.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is the edible nut of a North American hickory tree, used in pies.

clue.text: Heroes' lunch - a soup full of bones

definitions.note: describes the place; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: a soup is a mixture in which everything is stirred together, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hero's midday meal of bony broth.
explanation.definitionFit: A charnel house is a vault or building where human skeletal remains are stored.

clue.text: Loathsome leader with blemish surrounding his name

definitions.text: Loathsome leader with blemish surrounding his name

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only its first letter is kept
one word wraps itself round the other, holding it inside

blocks.note: a stain is a mark or blemish
the opening letter of the adjective

explanation.surface: A detested dictator whose very name carries a stain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the Soviet dictator; read as wordplay, the first letter of Loathsome sits inside a blemish, and the stained name is his.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin, the Soviet dictator responsible for purges and famine, is widely regarded as a hateful ruler.

clue.text: Passes into the river - and most with it

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: passes away, dies
the Trent is a major English river

explanation.surface: Someone drowns in the river, and the most fashionable too.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a long river through the English Midlands; passes means passes away.
explanation.definitionFit: With it is slang for fashionable, so most with it is the superlative of trendy.

clue.text: Boy found with unknown woman

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
algebra uses y for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A young man is seen in the company of a mysterious woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is a polite word for any woman, a female adult.

clue.text: Girl hearing sound of bell

indicators.note: hearing points to the ear, so the word is judged by pronunciation

blocks.note: the tolling of a bell, especially at a funeral

explanation.surface: A girl listens to a church bell ringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell is a girl's name, short for Helen or Eleanor.

clue.text: Visionary professional?

blocks.note: surface reading: an expert with imaginative foresight, a dreamer at the top of their field
setter's reading: someone whose profession concerns eyesight and spectacles

explanation.walkthrough: Visionary normally means far-sighted in ideas; here it means concerned with vision, the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician tests eyesight and supplies glasses and contact lenses, so their professional field is literally vision.

clue.text: People led astray by a botanist

indicators.note: something gone astray has wandered off its proper course, so these letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: men, people in general
taken as written before being scrambled

explanation.surface: A group of people misled by some plant expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregor Mendel, the monk who bred pea plants and founded genetics, worked as a botanist.

clue.text: Bird gets dodgy reward for a screw

indicators.note: something dodgy is unsound or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: doing bird is British slang for serving time in jail
taken as written before being scrambled

explanation.surface: A bird is given a suspicious payment in exchange for a screw.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is rhyming slang (birdlime, time) for a prison sentence, and screw is British slang for a jailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British criminal slang for a guard who locks up the inmates in a jail.

clue.text: Modern name for city with a bridge problem

definitions.text: Modern name for city with a bridge problem

blocks.note: surface reading: a town whose river crossing is congested or crumbling
setter's reading: the famous mathematical puzzle of the Seven Bridges of Königsberg, solved by Euler

explanation.walkthrough: Euler's Königsberg bridges problem founded graph theory; the city was renamed after the Soviet Union took it in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Königsberg, the Prussian city of the seven bridges puzzle, now belongs to Russia under its current Soviet-era name.

clue.text: A prig feels awkward at mickey-taking

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy and out of place, so these letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prudish person is uncomfortable when being teased.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the mickey is British slang for teasing or mocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Persiflage is light, frivolous banter and teasing, the gentle mockery that taking the mickey describes.

clue.text: Race is set with one old king mounted...

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means going upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Roman numeral for one
Shakespeare's aged king of Britain

explanation.surface: A race is arranged and an ancient king rides in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the part after 'is' climbs: set, one and the old king together are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Israelites, descendants of Jacob in the Bible, are a people, an ethnic group or race.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about a publication in Ulster

definitions.note: the answer is a town in Ulster

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation is placed round the other piece

blocks.note: an exclamation of surprise
short for magazine

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at a magazine they come across in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is simply a place found in Ulster, the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Omagh is the county town of Tyrone, located in Northern Ireland within the historic province.

clue.text: ... zealous one of the 14 has an idea - for negotiation?

indicators.note: something up for negotiation can be bargained into a different shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A devout member of a people has a proposal worth bargaining over.
explanation.walkthrough: The 14 points to the answer at 14 down, the biblical people; the ellipsis links the two clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hasidaeans were a pious Jewish sect of the Maccabean era, zealous devotees of the Law.

clue.text: De la Mare's audience

blocks.note: surface reading: the people who read or heard the poet Walter de la Mare
setter's reading: the title of his best-known poem, about a traveller knocking at an empty house

explanation.walkthrough: Walter de la Mare's most famous poem is about the phantom presences that hear a traveller knock at a silent door.
explanation.definitionFit: Any audience is made up of people paying attention by ear, and it is also the title of the poem.

clue.text: What guest without wedding garment does to get rebuke?

definitions.text: What guest without wedding garment does

blocks.clueFragment: What guest without wedding garment does
blocks.note: first meaning: wears casual clothes, as the guest in the parable who came improperly attired
second meaning: to scold someone severely

explanation.surface: The badly dressed wedding guest of Jesus's parable is told off by the king.
explanation.walkthrough: In Matthew 22 the guest without a wedding garment is thrown out, so dressing casually and being scolded go together.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to wear informal clothes and to reprimand someone harshly.

clue.text: Musical drama cost a bundle

indicators.note: things bundled together are thrown in a heap, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An opera production that was very expensive to stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cost a bundle' reads as a phrase for being expensive; bundle is the signal, not part of the price.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera about the singer Floria Tosca is a dramatic work set to music.

clue.text: Unpleasant fluids pouring over palate

indicators.note: fluids that are pouring are on the move and spilling, so these letters are mixed up
the liquid flows over and round the other piece so that it ends up enclosed

blocks.note: taken as written before being scrambled
palate, a sense of taste

explanation.surface: Nasty liquids washing over your tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distasteful is offensive or disagreeable, so unpleasant is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: It sometimes comes under the hammer

definitions.text: It sometimes comes under the hammer

blocks.note: surface reading: an item sold at auction
setter's reading: the digit that gets hit when a hammer misses the nail

explanation.walkthrough: Under the hammer is an idiom for being auctioned; literally, it is the part of the hand most often struck while hammering.
explanation.definitionFit: When holding a nail, a person's short broad digit is often struck by a badly aimed blow.

clue.text: Tart gets help to entrap church leader

indicators.note: to entrap is to catch and hold inside, so one piece is placed within the other
the leader of a word is its front letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: aid is help
the opening letter of church

explanation.surface: A loose woman gets assistance in seducing a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: Tart looks like a noun for a pastry or a woman, but it is an adjective meaning sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid as an adjective means sour or sharp-tasting, just as a tart flavour is.

clue.text: Bucks perhaps said to be over-valued

indicators.note: said means spoken out, so the pronunciation is what matters

blocks.note: dear means expensive, overpriced

explanation.surface: Dollars are said to be worth less than people think.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks looks like dollars; it means male animals, with perhaps marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is the male of several antlered animals such as the fallow, so bucks are an example of these.

clue.text: A yarn told without sympathy

indicators.note: something told is spoken out, so it is the pronunciation that counts

blocks.note: pitiless, lacking compassion

explanation.surface: A story recounted heartlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Yarn suggests a tale, which suits 'told'; here it is a kind of wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a thin worsted wool thread used for embroidery and tapestry.

clue.text: Stork frequently seen in a mess

blocks.note: first meaning: a large Asian stork with a bare head
second meaning: a military officer who would dine in the officers' mess

explanation.surface: A messy bird spotted often among clutter.
explanation.walkthrough: A mess is the dining room of military officers, not a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjutant stork is named for its stiff military gait, and an adjutant is a staff officer who uses the regimental mess.

clue.text: It's brave to dress in drag

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or set in order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wearing women's clothes as a man takes courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress in drag' reads as cross-dressing; dress is the signal and the next two words are the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring person is bold and fearless, willing to take risks, which is what being brave means.

clue.text: To ban fashion in dress is dull

definitions.note: adjective for a noun answer, read as 'is dull' = dullness

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape it anew, so these letters are remade
the reworked letters are put inside the garment word

blocks.note: taken as written before being scrambled
taken as written

explanation.surface: Outlawing style in clothing makes for boring outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Drabness is dreariness, a lack of colour and interest, the quality of being dull.
